item.title: New SNAP Eligibility Changes Could Leave Thousands of Immigrants, Refugees Without Food Assistance
item.description: Camilla Forte/Borderless Magazine/Catchlight Local/Report for AmericaOfficials are working to connect individuals with food assistance as over 340,000 Illinois residents — including 14,000 legally present immigrants with humanitarian protections — could lose SNAP benefits amid new eligibility changes.

item.title: SNAP 2026: What To Know About New Federal Changes
item.description: Camilla Forte/Borderless Magazine/Catchlight Local/Report for AmericaNew work eligibility rules for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, known as SNAP, is set to start Feb. 1. Borderless Magazine breaks down who's still eligible, what to know about these changes and what immigrants can do now.

item.title: Mayor Puts ‘ICE On Notice,’ Calling On Chicago Police To Investigate Crimes By Federal Agents
item.description: Colin Boyle/Block Club ChicagoThe ‘ICE On Notice’ executive order provides a framework for police and the Mayor’s Office to document and investigate alleged wrongdoing by immigration officers so they can be held criminally accountable, Mayor Brandon Johnson’s office said.

item.title: Between Two Countries: Inside A Venezuelan Woman’s Journey To Find Safety
item.description: Illustration by Jen Chavez for Borderless MagazineFearing deportation in Chicago, a Venezuelan national returned to her home country, but Maduro’s capture made her once again uncertain about her future and safety.

item.title: As Detentions Increase, Support from Chicago’s Consulates Varies for Immigrants Facing Deportation
item.description: Camilla Forte/Borderless Magazine/Catchlight Local/Report for AmericaSome consulates invest fewer resources into supporting nationals in the U.S., leaving some immigrants feeling unsupported as they face an increasingly harsh immigration system.

item.title: Federal Judge Rules Against ICE Over Memo That Expanded Power To Make Warrantless Arrests
item.description: Francia Garcia Hernandez/Block Club ChicagoU.S. District Judge Jeffrey Cummings ruled that immigration agents must follow the Castañon Nava consent decree, which is still in effect.

item.title: Meet the Chicago Students on the Frontlines of Walkouts
item.description: Max Herman/Borderless MagazineThe walkout is part of a series of student protests across Chicago amid a surge in immigration enforcement under President Donald Trump.

item.title: Mexican Father Who Signed for Voluntary Departure Didn’t Know He Had a Chance to Stay
item.description: Camilla Forte/Borderless Magazine/Catchlight Local/Report for AmericaVoluntary departures have skyrocketed under Trump, leading some attorneys to question whether immigrants are being coerced into agreeing to the alternative to deportation.

item.title: Illinois Man Whose Father Was Detained Attends Trump’s State of the Union
item.description: Kenny Holston/Pool via CNP/Sipa USA/Alamy Live NewsJaime Jr.’s father was arrested and taken to Mexico during Operation Midway Blitz in Chicago, leaving him to care for his teenage siblings.

item.title: Illinois Families, Child Care Providers on Edge Following Trump Funding Freeze
item.description: Photo illustration by Max Herman/Borderless Magazine. Source images: Zoonar/Morozova Tatiana/Alamy and State of IllinoisWhile the funds have not been permanently cut, advocates say the impact is threatening Illinois families, creating uncertainty for the future of some immigrant-run childcare facilities.
